rulings.Case Title: ZAIRE HILL VS. CITY AND COUNTY OF SAN FRANCISCO ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: MOTION FOR SUMMARY ADJUDICATION On First And Second Causes Of Action Alleged In Cross-Complaint
rulings.Rulings: Real Property/Housing Court Law and Motion Calendar for September 15, 2026. Line 1. CROSS COMPLAINANT CITY AND COUNTY OF SAN FRANCISCO MOTION FOR SUMMARY ADJUDICATION On First And Second Causes Of Action Alleged In Cross-Complaint is DENIED with prejudice. Moving party failed to shift their burden. Cross-Defendant's objections to evidence are sustained. The Court also notes that moving party appears to seek "summary adjudication... in the form of declaratory judgment" on the causes of action that are not for declaratory relief. The fifth cause of action for declaratory relief is not mentioned anywhere in the Notice of Motion. rulings.Case Title: MARK GIRAUDO VS. KATHERINE M. PAPAGEORGE ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion And Motion To Set Aside July 30, 2026 Default As Void Under Code Of Civil Procedure Section 473(D), Or Alternatively Under Section 473(B); To Preserve Status Quo Pending Determination; And For Related Relief
rulings.Rulings: Real Property/Housing Court Law and Motion Calendar for September 15, 2026. Line 5. DEFENDANT KATHERINE PAPAGEORGE INDIVIDUALLY AND AS SUCCESSOR TRUSTEE OF THE 1996 PAPAGEORGE FAMILY TRUST Notice Of Motion And Motion To Set Aside July 30, 2026 Default As Void Under Code Of Civil Procedure Section 473(D), Or Alternatively Under Section 473(B); To Preserve Status Quo Pending Determination; And For Related Relief is OFF CALENDAR. This motion was previously continued from September 9, 2026 for Defendant to comply with LRSF 2.7B and provide courtesy copies of the moving papers no later than September 10, 2026 with a cover letter reflecting the new hearing date. The papers subsequently provided by Defendant consisted only of the Notice of Errata and Supplemental Exhibits filed on September 3, 2026, and none of the original moving papers. In Defendant's Notice of Errata filed September 3, 2026, after and in response to opposition, Defendant admits that her moving papers, as originally filed, were not complete and that the motion was not made on proper notice. These substantial defects are beyond the scope of a simple typographical error or other minor defects that may be addressed by a notice of errata. The Supplemental Exhibits filed on September 3, 2026, served by mail only three court days before the original hearing date, are stricken as untimely. rulings.Case Title: LAN LE VS. BAI TIAN TAN ET AL
rulings.Rulings: Real Property/Housing Court Law and Motion Calendar for September 15, 2026. Line 9. DEFENDANT BAI TAN, MIAOQIN XU DEMURRER to COMPLAINT is SUSTAINED WITHOUT LEAVE TO AMEND. The Complaint is not uncertain regarding Plaintiff's claimed right to possession of the premises or right to pursue this action in her own name (i.e. standing). Defendants' arguments on this point regarding information that is not alleged appear to ignore the face of the Exhibits, which are incorporated into the Complaint. However, the demurrer of Defendant Xu is sustained on the sole basis that the Complaint does not include any allegation of service of the 60-Day Notice of Temporary Displacement on her. Regarding Plaintiff's argument in opposition, the Complaint does not allege that Defendant Xu is a co-tenant, but rather a subtenant. This distinction is consistent with the Lease attached to the Complaint, which is not signed by Defendant Xu and does not identify her as one of the "Tenants" under that Lease. The reasoning of University of Southern California v. Weiss (1962) 208 Cal.App.2d 759, 769-770 [citing Gentry v. Citron (1918) 36 Cal.App. 288], cited by Plaintiff in opposition, is therefore inapplicable to this case. The Court also notes that item 10.b. on the Judicial Council Form UD-100 Complaint makes it clear that such reasoning only applies to defendants who signed a joint written rental agreement, and Plaintiff appears to have understood this limitation as she did not check this box.=(501/CFH) Parties may appear in-person, telephonically or via Zoom (Video - Webinar ID: 160 560 5023; Password: 172849; or Phone Dial in: (669) 254-5252; Webinar ID: 160 560 5023; Password: 172849).
